## Slices

- Held-out (OOD) domains ['cooking', 'takeaway']: rows per split {'train': 3752, 'dev': 679, 'test': 1014}. Train/dev rows of these domains are never used for fitting or tuning; test rows are the OOD set.
- Human-judged code-mixed native rows (majority of MASSIVE judges said target+English): {('train', 'bn'): 1451, ('train', 'hi'): 608, ('dev', 'bn'): 265, ('dev', 'hi'): 110, ('test', 'bn'): 341, ('test', 'hi'): 144}
- Side-effect rate among in-domain rows: train 32.6%, dev 31.1%, test 33.8%

## Label provenance

- `scenario`, `intent`: human annotation from MASSIVE (validated by 3 judges per utterance).
- `side_effect`: deterministic mapping from the human intent via `configs/side_effects.yaml`.
- `native` text: professional human translation. `romanized`, `codemix`, `codemix_romanized`: synthetic, rule-generated, labels inherited from the source id (no model in the loop).
- Headline metrics are reported on human-translated `native` test rows; synthetic slices are robustness probes only and are never the sole evaluation set.
